title: MERSIT: A Hardware-Efficient 8-bit Data Format with Enhanced Post-Training Quantization DNN Accuracy
problem: Post-training quantization (PTQ) models using conventional 8-bit Integer or floating-point formats suffer significant accuracy degradation in modern DNNs. Current 8-bit quantization approaches are unreliable for practical deployment.
motivation: 8-bit quantization is essential for efficient DNN inference in resource-constrained hardware, but maintaining accuracy during quantization remains a critical challenge for real-world deployment.
method: MERSIT is an 8-bit number format designed to compress neural networks while preserving accuracy. It works by flexibly dividing bits between the exponent (the "scale") and fraction (the "precision") portions, adapting an idea from the Posit number format. To make this work efficiently in hardware, it combines the decoding steps into a single optimized process, called a "merged decoding scheme," which reduces the chip area and power needed compared to previous approaches. This format is tested across different types of neural networks to measure both accuracy and hardware performance.
key_novelty: MERSIT is an 8-bit compression format with dynamic exponent/fraction-bit configuration (inspired by Posit) and a merged hardware-efficient decoding scheme.
contributions: MERSIT: novel 8-bit PTQ data format with Posit-inspired dynamic bit configuration
Merged decoding scheme achieving 26.6% area savings and 22.2% power reduction vs Posit-based units
Superior accuracy across various DNNs compared to conventional 8-bit Integer and floating-point formats
Hardware-efficient processing unit design maintaining floating-point-equivalent efficiency

metrics.accuracy: superior across various DNNs vs conventional 8-bit formats

limitations: Specific DNN models tested, comparison with other recent PTQ methods, and scope of "various DNNs" not detailed in abstract.
primary_theme: Efficient 8-bit quantization via dynamic data format
